L16: ## 49.8 The Dedekind different
L17: 
L18: Let $A \to B$ be a ring map. We say the Dedekind different is defined if $A$ is Noetherian, $A \to B$ is finite, any nonzerodivisor on $A$ is a nonzerodivisor on $B$, and $K \to L$ is étale where $K = Q(A)$ and $L = B \otimes _ A K$. Then $K \subset L$ is finite étale and
L19: 
L20: \[ \mathcal{L}_{B/A} = \{ x \in L \mid \text{Trace}_{L/K}(bx) \in A \text{ for all }b \in B\} \]
L21: 
L22: is the Dedekind complementary module. In this situation the Dedekind different is
L23: \[ \mathfrak {D}_{B/A} = \{ x \in L \mid x\mathcal{L}_{B/A} \subset B\} \]
L24: 
L25: viewed as a $B$-submodule of $L$. By Lemma 【11†49.8.1】 the Dedekind different is an ideal of $B$ either if $A$ is normal or if $B$ is flat over $A$.
L26: 
L27: 【11†Lemma 49.8.1.】 Assume the Dedekind different of $A \to B$ is defined. Consider the statements
L28: 
L29:   1. $A \to B$ is flat,
L30: 
L31:   2. $A$ is a normal ring,
L32: 
L33:   3. $\text{Trace}_{L/K}(B) \subset A$,
L34: 
L35:   4. $1 \in \mathcal{L}_{B/A}$, and
L36:   5. the Dedekind different $\mathfrak {D}_{B/A}$ is an ideal of $B$.
L37: 
L38: Then we have (1) $\Rightarrow $ (3), (2) $\Rightarrow $ (3), (3) $\Leftrightarrow $ (4), and (4) $\Rightarrow $ (5).
L39: 
L40: Proof. The equivalence of (3) and (4) and the implication (4) $\Rightarrow $ (5) are immediate.
L41: 
L42: If $A \to B$ is flat, then we see that $\text{Trace}_{B/A} : B \to A$ is defined and that $\text{Trace}_{L/K}$ is the base change. Hence (3) holds.

L23: 【8†Theorem 53.2.6.】 Let $k$ be a field. The following categories are canonically equivalent
L24: 
L25:   1. The category of finitely generated field extensions $K/k$ of transcendence degree $1$.
L26: 
L27:   2. The category of curves and dominant rational maps.
L28: 
L29:   3. The category of normal projective curves and nonconstant morphisms.
L30: 
L31:   4. The category of nonsingular projective curves and nonconstant morphisms.
L32: 
L33:   5. The category of regular projective curves and nonconstant morphisms.
L34:   6. The category of normal proper curves and nonconstant morphisms.
L35: 
L36: Proof. The equivalence between categories (1) and (2) is the restriction of the equivalence of Varieties, Theorem 【15†33.4.1】. Namely, a variety is a curve if and only if its function field has transcendence degree $1$, see for example Varieties, Lemma 【16†33.20.3】.
L37: The categories in (3), (4), (5), and (6) are the same. First of all, the terms “regular” and “nonsingular” are synonyms, see Properties, Definition 【17†28.9.1】. Being normal and regular are the same thing for Noetherian $1$-dimensional schemes (Properties, Lemmas 【18†28.9.4】 and 【19†28.12.6】). See Varieties, Lemma 【20†33.43.8】 for the case of curves. Thus (3) is the same as (5). Finally, (6) is the same as (3) by Varieties, Lemma 【21†33.43.4】.

L22: 【8†Definition 42.10.2.】 Let $(S, \delta )$ be as in Situation 【14†42.7.1】. Let $X$ be locally of finite type over $S$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module.
L23: 
L24:   1. For any irreducible component $Z' \subset \text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ with generic point $\xi $ the integer $m_{Z', \mathcal{F}} = \text{length}_{\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi }} \mathcal{F}_\xi $ (Lemma 【10†42.10.1】) is called the multiplicity of $Z'$ in $\mathcal{F}$.
L25:   2. Assume $\dim _\delta (\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})) \leq k$. The $k$-cycle associated to $\mathcal{F}$ is
L26: 
L27: \[ [\mathcal{F}]_ k = \sum m_{Z', \mathcal{F}}[Z'] \]

L16: ## 59.79 Cohomology with support in a closed subscheme
L17: 
L18: Let $X$ be a scheme and let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\acute{e}tale}$. We let
L19: 
L20: \[ \Gamma _ Z(X, \mathcal{F}) = \{ s \in \mathcal{F}(X) \mid \text{Supp}(s) \subset Z\} \]
L21: 
L22: be the sections with support in $Z$ (Definition 【11†59.31.3】). This is a left exact functor which is not exact in general. Hence we obtain a derived functor
L23: \[ R\Gamma _ Z(X, -) : D(X_{\acute{e}tale}) \longrightarrow D(\textit{Ab}) \]
L24: 
L25: and cohomology groups with support in $Z$ defined by $H^ q_ Z(X, \mathcal{F}) = R^ q\Gamma _ Z(X, \mathcal{F})$.
L26: Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an injective abelian sheaf on $X_{\acute{e}tale}$. Let $U = X \setminus Z$. Then the restriction map $\mathcal{I}(X) \to \mathcal{I}(U)$ is surjective (Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 【12†21.12.6】) with kernel $\Gamma _ Z(X, \mathcal{I})$. It immediately follows that for $K \in D(X_{\acute{e}tale})$ there is a distinguished triangle
L27: 
L28: \[ R\Gamma _ Z(X, K) \to R\Gamma (X, K) \to R\Gamma (U, K) \to R\Gamma _ Z(X, K)[1] \]
L29: in $D(\textit{Ab})$. As a consequence we obtain a long exact cohomology sequence
L30: 
L31: \[ \ldots \to H^ i_ Z(X, K) \to H^ i(X, K) \to H^ i(U, K) \to H^{i + 1}_ Z(X, K) \to \ldots \]
L32: 
L33: for any $K$ in $D(X_{\acute{e}tale})$.
L34: 
L35: For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X_{\acute{e}tale}$ we can consider the subsheaf of sections with support in $Z$, denoted $\mathcal{H}_ Z(\mathcal{F})$, defined by the rule
L36: 
L37: \[ \mathcal{H}_ Z(\mathcal{F})(U) = \{ s \in \mathcal{F}(U) \mid \text{Supp}(s) \subset U \times _ X Z\} \]
